_about: Maps every run outcome OpenAdapt emits to one plain result.
The plain result comes from the precise outcome (transaction_outcome or the Execute terminal outcome), never from the coarse HALTED label alone.
Only an outcome that proves no effect sets may_have_changed=false and safe_to_retry=true.
safe_to_retry means a new attempt can't duplicate or collide with a write from this attempt. It doesn't promise the new attempt will succeed.
openadapt_types.plain_results applies these rules in Python. Other languages apply the same merge_rules and check themselves against outcome-vectors.json.

emitters.symbol: openadapt_flow/runner/hosted_adapter.py HostedTerminalEventV1.outcome and HostedTerminalEventV2.outcome. Pass started as dispatched and uncertain_delivery as delivery_uncertain.
openadapt_flow/ir.py RunReport.terminal_outcome and State.outcome. This is where the program graph ended, not the Execute terminal outcome.
openadapt_types/control_overlay.py ControlOverlayPhase (control_overlay.py ControlOverlayFrameV1.phase and control_overlay_tracking.py ControlOverlayFrameV2.phase)

openadapt_flow/runtime/control_overlay.py RuntimeControlOverlayEmitter. emit_terminal maps RunReport.execution_outcome one to one onto the five end phases; runtime/replayer.py emits observing, executing, and verifying during a run.

The outcome of the step that ended a multi-step process. An earlier step may already have saved, so halted_before_effect, rejected_policy, or failed_platform here doesn't prove the process wrote nothing. Never pass it as execute_terminal_outcome.

done.label: Done and checked
done.meaning: It saved the entry and read the record back to confirm it.

stopped_before_change.label: Stopped before saving
stopped_before_change.meaning: Something didn't match, so it stopped before changing anything and asked a person. Nothing was written.

check_the_record.label: Check the record
check_the_record.meaning: A save may have gone through. A person checks the record before anything is retried.

finished_not_checked.label: Finished, not checked
finished_not_checked.meaning: It did the steps but didn't confirm the saved result.

did_not_finish.label: Didn't finish
did_not_finish.meaning: It couldn't complete the task. The next step says what's known about whether anything was written.

refused.label: Blocked before saving
refused.meaning: A rule, an approval, or the right-record check blocked the run before it saved anything. Nothing was written.

sealed.label: Signed receipt
sealed.meaning: OpenAdapt signed a receipt that records what was entered and how it was checked.

local.label: Local run report
local.meaning: A run report on the computer that ran it. OpenAdapt didn't sign it.

none.label: No receipt
none.meaning: Only the status itself backs this result.

merge_rules: 1. Ignore any input whose value is listed in not_an_outcome for its source.
2. Use only the first tier in tiers that still has an input. Ignore the lower tiers, except for rule 4.

3. Each input in that tier selects one row from sources.<source>.values. A value listed under in_progress.<source> selects no row and marks the run as still in progress. A value with no row selects fallbacks.unrecognized and ends the merge.
4. When transaction_outcome and execution_outcome are both present, execution_outcome must appear in that transaction row's execution_outcomes list. Otherwise use fallbacks.conflict.
5. A row with if_not_dispatched uses that variant only when the caller states dispatched=false.

6. If the tier marks the run as in progress and selects no row, there's no result yet: report in_progress.execute_state.<state>. For an execute_state input, <state> is the value itself. For any other source, it's the state that the value's in_progress entry names. If the tier also selects a row, or marks the run as in progress twice, use fallbacks.conflict.
7. Rows that agree on result: use the most cautious row, which is the first in precedence order with may_have_changed=true, else the first with safe_to_retry=false, else the first.
8. Rows that disagree on result: if every row has may_have_changed=false, use the first in precedence order. Otherwise use fallbacks.conflict.
9. delivery_uncertain=true turns any result except check_the_record into fallbacks.delivery_uncertain.
10. No input at all selects fallbacks.missing.
11. proof defaults to none. proof=sealed needs an execute_terminal_outcome, because a signed receipt always carries one.

transaction_outcome.meaning: Flow's terminal transaction outcome: what the evidence proves about the business effect.

VERIFIED.next_action: Nothing else to do. OpenAdapt read the record back and it matches.

HALTED_BEFORE_EFFECT.next_action: Nothing was written. Look at why it stopped, fix that, then run it again.

RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED.next_action: A save may have gone through. Check the record before anyone runs this again.

FAILED_PLATFORM.next_action: OpenAdapt hit a problem before it changed anything, so nothing was written. You can run it again.

CANCELED.next_action: Someone canceled the run before it changed anything, so nothing was written. Run it again when you're ready.

REJECTED_POLICY.next_action: Nothing was written. A rule, an approval, or the right-record check blocked this run. Fix that, then run it again.

SAVED_AWAITING_CHECK.next_action: It saved the entry and is waiting for the later report that confirms it. Don't run it again; it counts as done only when that report does.

COMPLETED_UNVERIFIED.next_action: The steps ran, but nothing confirmed the saved result. Check the record before you count it as done or run it again.

ROLLED_BACK.next_action: OpenAdapt found an extra change and undid it. Check the record before anyone runs this again.
